question: Why do ORAL Surveillance and STAR-RA appear to reach different conclusions about cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib?

claims.text: ORAL Surveillance enrolled patients 50 years or older with cardiovascular risk factors, while STAR-RA included broader real-world RA patients.
claims.reason: Quoted words do not match the cited passage.

claims.text: STAR-RA included a real-world evidence cohort and an RCT-duplicate cohort mimicking ORAL Surveillance criteria to calibrate results.

citations.quote: (2) A 'randomised controlled trial (RCT)-duplicate cohort' mimicking inclusion and exclusion criteria of the ORAL surveillance trial to calibrate results

claims.reason: STAR-RA created two cohorts: a real-world evidence cohort and an RCT-duplicate cohort mimicking ORAL Surveillance inclusion/exclusion criteria to calibrate results against the trial findings (pmid-35027405-e31c1e0e2f).

claims.text: ORAL Surveillance was a randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial with adjudicated MACE and cancer endpoints.

citations.quote: We conducted a randomized, open-label, noninferiority, postauthorization, safety end-point trial involving patients with active rheumatoid arthritis

claims.reason: ORAL Surveillance was a randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial involving patients with active rheumatoid arthritis 50 years or older with cardiovascular risk factors, with adjudicated MACE and cancer endpoints (pmid-35081280-b8cafa5357).

claims.text: STAR-RA used observational claims data with propensity score weighting to estimate hazard ratios for cardiovascular outcomes.
claims.reason: STAR-RA used observational claims data and applied Cox proportional hazards models with propensity score fine stratification weighting to estimate hazard ratios for cardiovascular outcomes (pmid-35027405-e31c1e0e2f).

claims.text: ORAL Surveillance found higher MACE risk with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors in a cardiovascular risk-enriched population.
claims.reason: ORAL Surveillance found higher risks of MACE and cancers with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors in a cardiovascular risk-enriched population, not meeting noninferiority criteria (pmid-35081280-3df021ee3e).

claims.text: STAR-RA found no significant increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib in routine care patients but a non-significant increased risk in cardiovascular risk patients.
claims.reason: STAR-RA found no significant increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib in routine care patients but observed a non-significant increased risk in patients with cardiovascular risk factors (pmid-35027405-1e63b57282).

answer: STAR-RA included a real-world evidence cohort and an RCT-duplicate cohort mimicking ORAL Surveillance criteria to calibrate results. ORAL Surveillance was a randomized, open-label, noninferiority trial with adjudicated MACE and cancer endpoints. STAR-RA used observational claims data with propensity score weighting to estimate hazard ratios for cardiovascular outcomes. ORAL Surveillance found higher MACE risk with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors in a cardiovascular risk-enriched population. STAR-RA found no significant increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib in routine care patients but a non-significant increased risk in cardiovascular risk patients.
limitations: STAR-RA observational design cannot establish causality unlike randomized ORAL Surveillance trial.
Differences in patient populations and inclusion criteria limit direct comparability of results.
STAR-RA's non-significant findings do not prove absence of cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib.
Full-text details of STAR-RA and ORAL Surveillance methodologies are not available in abstracts, limiting detailed comparison.
